subject: Post-demo sync: parity probe plan & hallucination regression checks
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodhq.com>
To: Ethan Foster <ethan.foster@synthoria.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodhq.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodhq.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Oct 2027 15:23:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo follow-up + parity probe proposal

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get you the parity numbers you asked for: 

• Goal: run a short, reproducible parity probe comparing the critical signals you care about across Synthoria’s current inference endpoints (AWS/GCP) and Redwood hosted inference. We’ll measure latency (p50/p95), token cost per request, and a small set of quality metrics (hallucination rate, factuality score on the prompt set, and answer conciseness).

• Suggested probe scope (attached: synthoria-probe-matrix.xlsx):
  - 250 representative prompts (you can supply a seed sample or we can use a masked subset of your QA corpus)
  - 3 runtime configs: production-sized prompt lengths, an edge-case long-context set, and a stress batch mode for throughput numbers
  - Model variants: your current hyperscaler config (please confirm model id), Redwood-verified open model equivalent, and a quantized variant we can spin up in the hosted sandbox

• Immediate asks from you:
  1) A sample of 200-300 prompts (PII scrubbed) or instructions for us to pull a masked set from your corpus
  2) Preferred hyperscaler endpoints + any API keys we can use in a read-only sandbox mode (we can also run from your side if preferred)
  3) Any specific hallucination cases you hate (e.g., dates, phone numbers, financial figures) so we can include targeted probes

We can run the initial probe on Redwood hosted (fast turnaround) and then replicate on a Dedicated node if you want identical hardware. Attached is a short probe matrix — if you can fill the red fields and return, we’ll schedule a 2–3 hour run next week and deliver a concise delta report.

Next step: are you available for a 30-minute alignment on Tue 2027-10-12 14:00 PT? If not, suggest two slots and we’ll accommodate.

Attachments: synthoria-probe-matrix.xlsx (attachment stub)

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodhq.com | +1 415-555-0182

--
On behalf of Redwood — we typically look at hallucination rates using a small curated prompt set and a second masked factuality set (both included in the probe matrix). Will share a short runbook and Drive link when we lock the slot.

From: Ethan Foster <ethan.foster@synthoria.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodhq.com>
Cc: Priya Sen <priya.sen@synthoria.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up + parity probe proposal

Vanessa — thanks, that looks great. A few clarifying Qs before we push data: 

1) For the hyperscaler model ids, we currently use a fine-tuned gpt-4x-lite equivalent on AWS and a tuned Vertex endpoint on GCP. Is it OK if we provide read-only keys and you run the calls from your Redwood sandbox (we'd prefer that for reproducibility)?
2) For hallucination metrics: do you use automated NLI-based checks or human labeling for the initial pass? Rough cost/time expectations for a 250-prompt probe?
3) We can share a sample CSV. I attached a small config (sample_config.json) that shows our internal prompt format.

Also, Priya and I noted a few items the product team wanted to see: can you include a short section in the delta report that calls out where batching/kv-cache behavior materially changes latency during multi-turn prompts?

We can do Tue 10/12 14:00 PT — sending a calendar invite shortly.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Foster
Head of ML Platforms | Synthoria Inc.
ethan.foster@synthoria.com | +1 617-555-0147

Attachment: sample_config.json (attachment stub)

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodhq.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodhq.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up + parity probe proposal — slot confirmed

Perfect — invite received, thanks Ethan. Quick answers to your questions and a few attachments/links so your infra team can prep: 

1) Hyperscaler keys: running from our hosted sandbox is fine and is easiest to keep runs consistent; we will treat any keys as ephemeral and purge after the probe. If you prefer to run on your side, we will provide the exact call script.

2) Hallucination measurement: we start with automated heuristics (question-answer alignment + factuality NLI), then sample 10% for light human review to validate edge cases. For a 250-prompt probe we expect ~4–6 hours of automated runs and ~6–10 hours of light human pass if you opt in (we can do the human review on a smaller stratified sample).

3) Batching / KV-cache note: good call — we will include an explicit breakdown. For multi-turn prompts we’ll report per-step latency deltas and whether continuous batching impacted p95. Karthik will be the lead on measuring KV cache hit/miss effects during the multi-turn set.

Deliverables: short report (PDF) with charts, a CSV of raw per-request signals, and a short playbook of quick tuning levers (batching, quantization profile, route policy) tailored to your workload. Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cProbeMatrix
HubSpot: contact=hs_123456789

Attached: probe-instructions.pdf — includes the exact curl commands we’ll run and the expected response schema. For credentials we can use one-time presigned S3 upload or you can share a read-only key in the secure HubSpot note.

See you Tue — we'll kick the run right after the call and share an interim delta within 24 hours.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodhq.com

Attachment: probe-instructions.pdf (attachment stub)

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodhq.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2027 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo sync — quick tech notes before Tue run

Ethan — quick technical clarifications from my side before we start: 

• Auth & rate limits: please provide keys scoped for read-only inference with a 10 RPS per-key cap for the probe so we can fairly measure p95 under steady load. If you cannot throttle, let us know and we will run from your side and request logs.
• Payloads: our call script accepts the sample_config.json shape you sent; we’ll translate the prompt wrapper into the model-specific payloads for each hyperscaler.
• Measurement: p50/p95 token-level latency, token consumption, and a checksum of responses for deterministic comparison. For hallucination scoring we’ll run an NLI check followed by a 10% stratified human sample (we can send the human-labeling rubric if you want).

I’ll be on the call Tue and will own the KV-cache / multi-turn instrumentation. If we see large deltas we’ll add a quick canary that toggles batching and quantization profiles to surface quick wins.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodhq.com
